warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory. lockToken, lockNFT and splitLock are payable solely for protocol fees; other selected methods require zero native value.

Ethereum current Team Finance Lock proxy 0xe2fe530c047f2d85298b07d9333c05737f1435fb only, observed implementation 0x6dd27f2b82f78dd8a802a9228f340518280359f1. Sourcify proxy creation/runtime grades are match, while implementation grades are exact_match. EIP-1967 slot at block 26261007 agrees. paused() was false then; this is not live authorization or a permanent availability claim.

lockToken pulls caller-owned ERC20/LP tokens and records a time-locked internal deposit for the designated withdrawalAddress; actual credited amount is the vault token-balance increase, accommodating transfer fees but providing no minimum credited amount. Token amounts use native units. Withdrawal address is not checked nonzero by this body: an unusable recipient can strand the claim. Unlock time must be strictly in the future; no early withdrawal is provided.

lockNFT pulls only caller ERC721 tokenId, requires amount == 1 and future unlockTime, and records withdrawalAddress. Optional _mintNFT creates the protocol receipt NFT; it is not wallet/operator authorization, but adds dependency on the configured NFT contract. Standalone receipt mint and lock ownership transfers are not admitted. No arbitrary executable calldata, permit or backend signing is accepted.

Payable locks calculate native ETH fees through mutable estimator/USD-token settings and caller/token fee exemptions. Ordinary fee payment accepts up to 5% under quote; excess is refunded with a native call. Nonzero referrer cannot equal caller, requires configured discount and receives a configured fraction of the fee; referral and refund calls can fail. splitLock charges the ordinary non-referral fee. No fixed fee or refund success is promised.

extendLockDuration only extends an own unwithdrawn lock to a strictly later future timestamp. splitLock only divides an own ERC20 lock into two positive balances, with the new unlockTime no earlier than the original and same recorded withdrawal address. It cannot split a locked ERC721. If a receipt NFT exists, required current receipt ownership is checked in addition to the recorded withdrawal-address conditions.

withdrawTokens requires caller be the recorded withdrawal address, plus receipt-NFT ownership if minted, and waits until unlockTime. ERC20 withdrawals support positive partial amounts; full withdrawal clears the record and burns any receipt. For ERC721, _amount is ignored and the recorded tokenId is returned. Outputs go only to caller. Withdraw and extension do not have whenNotPaused; source guards are not assertions of current paused state.

collectUniswapV3LPFees requires caller be the recorded withdrawalAddress of an unwithdrawn NFT lock and invokes only the fixed collect tuple at that locked NFT contract, sending both fee assets to that same address with uint128 maximum amounts. There is no caller-supplied call payload; incompatible or malicious locked NFTs can revert or behave unexpectedly. Principal remains locked until maturity.

Proxy and owner powers are material: current implementation includes owner-only recoverAssets(user,newRecipient), which can reassign whole user deposit claims and burn receipts; ownership, fee configuration, pausing and upgrades remain mutable and are excluded. Marketing statements of noncustody do not override this source fact. The historical migration exploit is not admitted: current ABI has no migrate executor, and current primary pages explicitly offer ordinary new locks, splitting and partial claims, not recovery-only services.

devdoc.details: Extends from BaseAdminUpgradeabilityProxy with a constructor for  initializing the implementation, admin, and init data.

admin().return: The address of the proxy admin.

changeAdmin(address).details: Changes the admin of the proxy. Only the current admin can call this function.

params.newAdmin: Address to transfer proxy administration to.

params._data: Data to send as msg.data to the implementation to initialize the proxied contract. It should include the signature and the parameters of the function to be called, as described in https://solidity.readthedocs.io/en/v0.4.24/abi-spec.html#function-selector-and-argument-encoding. This parameter is optional, if no data is given the initialization call to proxied contract will be skipped.

upgradeTo(address).details: Upgrade the backing implementation of the proxy. Only the admin can call this function.

upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes).details: Upgrade the backing implementation of the proxy and call a function on the new implementation. This is useful to initialize the proxied contract.

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://handbook.team.finance/services/token-locks.md). # Token Locks Token locks involve a user sending tokens to a smart contract. While inside the contract, tokens cannot be traded or withdrawn. Tokens are released once the time period the token sender established is complete. This time-release is customizable, with the sender being able to choose the exact day and time they want the tokens to become available.\ \ Our token lockup smart contracts are decentralized (Team Finance has no ability to access the tokens inside) and support 15+ unique blockchains. All contracts are audited by leading security firms.\ \ **Lock your tokens in seconds**, and benefit from Team Finance's unique locking service features like Split Locks, Partial Claims, and Lock Transfers. ### Features

Split Locks

Split your main lock into smaller locks. These smaller locks can have different owner addresses and end dates.

Benefits:

  • Diversifies risk away from a single wallet address
  • Avoid minimum transaction amount limits when withdrawing tokens
  • $150 USD locking fee for each split lock.

Partial Claims

Withdraw any number of tokens from a lock, not just the full amount.

Benefits:

  • Avoid problems with minimum transaction amounts when withdrawing tokens
  • No additional costs to using partial claims, only the associated gas fees.

Lock Transfers

Transfer lock ownership of a lock to another wallet address.

Benefits:

  • Flexibility in case there are changes to the project team
  • No fee for transferring ownership of a lock.

How Team Finance Builds and Secures Its Smart Contracts

The foundation of every great project starts with secure smart contracts.

Team Finance

24 Jul 2025 • 2 min read
Share

Since 2022, Team Finance has been refining our infrastructure and development processes to create a stronger suite of products and smart contracts for our community. With safety and exploit reduction as our number one priority, here are some of the strategies we’ve used to allow projects to build confidently with Team Finance.

A Contract-First Approach

Every feature of Team Finance begins with the smart contract, helping our users launch safely and securely. But how do we know that our smart contracts are safe?

Here's how:

Audits From Web3’s Leading Firms

  • Contracts for Team Finance are audited by top industry infrastructure partners. These audits search for vulnerabilities and possible exploits before deploying the contract.

Open Source and Transparent

  • Our documentation portal enables developers to review our smart contracts directly. Trust comes from transparency.

Always Improving and Growing

  • Team Finance contracts are built with upgrades in mind. This allows us to adapt to security threats, increase performance, and enhance functions without having to go back to square one.

Our Core Smart Contracts and How They're Secured

🔐 Liquidity Locking

Liquidity Locks allow projects to securely lock their LP tokens across Web3 using our liquidity locking tool. These locks support a wide range of decentralized exchanges (DEXs) and blockchains, making it easy for teams to launch with confidence.

To ensure security, we implement multiple layers of protection, including:

  • Independent audits by trusted security firms
  • A clear, user-friendly dashboard for full transparency and control

🕒 Token Vesting Contracts

The Vesting Tools allow you to create time-based token releases for founders, teams, and community members.

  • All data is verifiable on-chain for maximum transparency
  • Wallet nicknames can be used to name your vesting wallets, making them easier to use.
  • Contracts are designed to prevent hacks, exploits, or early release

🛠️ Token Generation & Staking Contracts

Team Finance's Token Creation Tool and Staking Pools enable teams to launch tokens and expand their community with no coding required.

  • Token creation made simple with our wizard. Just complete the steps and create your token in just minutes.
  • Instant validation of contracts with reliable audits.
  • Tools designed for non-coders, by coders.

📤 MultiSender

The MultiSender enables airdrops and mass token transfers with ease.

  • Airdrop with confidence. Includes confirmation steps built into the UI to prevent misclicks or errors
  • Designed to reduce gas costs while maintaining on-chain visibility

Security is our Commitment

Since 2022, we’ve doubled down on security with major infrastructure and policy upgrades:

  • Audit Hosting MigrationWe transitioned our audit archive to a section in our GitBook documentation, allowing for easier access and a more professional presentation.
  • Proactive Code ReviewsRegular internal audits are done by our team to confirm findings and improve contract design.
  • Monitoring & FeedbackWe’ve implemented new internal systems to flag abnormal usage and push for real-time developer feedback.

Trusted by Web3

Over 35,000 projects have used Team Finance to lock liquidity, vest, and launch their tokens safely. Our tools have supported everything from meme coins to major DeFi protocols. What do they all have in common? A secure and battle-tested base powered by Team Finance smart contracts.

Explore Team Finance

If you’re a developer or team member looking to explore how our contracts work, we invite you to:

  • Review our GitBook
  • Join our official Telegram Channel
  • Connect with our team
  • Check out Team Finance to review our services

In Web3, you only get one shot to launch the right way. Launch with confidence. Launch with Team Finance.
